concepts.request: One JSON object per line over the control socket. Shape: {"id":<any scalar>,"op":"<verb>",...}. The id is echoed in the reply. Verbs: action, query, undo, redo, goto, save, load, transport, help, list_actions, describe_action, list_queries, describe_query, ping, shutdown.
concepts.response: {"id":..,"ok":true,"result":..} on success, or {"id":..,"ok":false,"error":{"code":..,"message":..}}. Codes: bad_json, bad_request, unknown_op, unknown_action, unknown_query, not_found, execution_failed, no_project.
concepts.managerPath: Addresses which graph to act on. [] is the root graph. [p] descends into the Patcher node with id p. [m,q] descends into patcher q of the Multiplexer node m. Paths nest further. Enumerate valid ones with the `managers` query.
concepts.nodeID: 0 is the Output node, 1 is the Input node. Anything else is a node you created with add_node. List them with the `nodes` query.
concepts.portID: Nodes own input/output ports, each with its own id. The `node` query lists them under inputs[]/outputs[] with dataType (0 = Events/MIDI, 1 = Waveform/audio) and connection state. Connections are (nodeID, portID) pairs.
concepts.undo: Every `action` is recorded in an undo tree, applied to the GUI graph and replayed on the audio graph. `undo`, `redo` and `goto` walk that tree; `goto` takes a child-index path from the root.
concepts.note pitch: pitchVector is a positional list of [num,den] exponent pairs over primes [2,3,5,7,11,13,...]: pitch = 69 + 12*log2(product(prime_i ^ (num_i/den_i))). [] is 1/1 = MIDI 69. The 5-limit ratio 5/4 is [[-2,1],[0,1],[1,1]].
concepts.note rhythm: rhythmVector / rhythmEndVector are the note's start and end in BEATS, as the same prime-exponent pairs: value = sum((num_i/den_i) * log2(prime_i)). [] is beat 0, [[1,1]] is beat 1, [[1,2]] is beat 0.5.
concepts.tuning: A region carries the scale. tuningMode 0 = harmonic lattice, 1 = EDO. In harmonic mode, tuningAnchorHarmonic is the anchor harmonic A and tuningHarmonicAnchorVector is that harmonic's pitch; lattice line h sits at anchorVec - dense(A) + dense(h), where dense(h) is h's prime factorisation. A note's tuningAnchorHarmonic is WHICH line it sits on (its scale degree) — not the region's anchor. A note's tuningMode is inherited from the region when the note is created.
concepts.degrees: Harmonic scale degrees are named by harmonic number: I = 1/2/4/8 (any power of two), II = 9, III = 5 or 10, IV = 4, V = 3 or 6, VI = 5 or 10, VII = 15.
concepts.transport position: beatPosition/timeSeconds are the transport ANCHOR (the seek target, set when playback starts). The live playhead is effectiveBeatPosition/effectiveTime, published from the audio thread. A playhead that looks stuck at the anchor is normal while playing — read the effective pair.
concepts.threading: Requests run on the GUI thread, so mutations always land on the authoritative graph copies and are mirrored to the audio graph. No request blocks audio.
concepts.read-live rule: Actions take INTENT, not state. You pass what you want; the DAW reads the current value itself (old parameter values, existing cables, the note's prior snapshot). Never send a value you read back earlier — it may be stale and will corrupt the undo entry.
concepts.arranger elements: An Arranger node holds elements and tracks. An ELEMENT is the content — a region (notes), an audio clip, or an automation curve; type 0/1/2 respectively. Regions, clips and curves SHARE one id space per arranger, so an element id is unambiguous. That same id is what you pass as elementID / regionID / curveID depending on the action.
concepts.positions: A POSITION is a placement of an element on a track at a time — separate from the element itself, and one element can have many. Keys: startOffsetPairs (extra start offset in beats, [] = 0), rhythmVector (start beat), rhythmEndVector (end beat), trackID, id (the positionID used by delete_position / move_element_position), plus rhythmEdo* snapshots. Get them from the `elements` or `region` query.
concepts.tracks: An Arranger track is {type, id, connectionID, inputConnectionID, recordArmed, monitor}. type 0 = Audio, 1 = Notes. connectionID is the track's output port on the Arranger node (Waveform for Audio, Events for Notes); inputConnectionID is its per-track input port on the same node, in track order. recordArmed makes the track capture its input while the transport plays and global record is on; monitor sums the input into the track output live. Get them from the `tracks` query.
concepts.automation curve points: A curve point is {timeVec, v, shape, shapeParam}. timeVec is the X position in BEATS, encoded exactly like note rhythm (value = sum((num_i/den_i)*log2(prime_i)); [] = beat 0, [[1,1]] = beat 1, [[9,1]] = beat 9). v is the value — BPM for the tempo curve, otherwise the target parameter's range. shape: 0 = Hold, 1 = Single (smooth bow), 2 = Double (smoother); shapeParam is -1..1, a bow amount for Single and a balance for Double.
concepts.embedded windows: Nodes are floating windows inside the canvas and have their own id space, SEPARATE from node ids: ewID comes from the editor's pool (0 and 1 are reserved, so on a fresh graph the Output node gets ewID 2 and the Input node ewID 3). Never compute it — read it from the `embedded_windows` query, and pass it to move_embedded_window / resize_embedded_window.
concepts.vst state blobs: compState / ctrlState in vst_state_change are base64 strings (standard alphabet, = padding) of the plugin's raw component/controller state. Get the current ones from the plugin, or pass neither to re-apply the current state.
concepts.undo tree: The `undo` query returns {head, version}. head is the root action; each node has type (an ActionType int), its action-specific fields, children[], name, last_index and optionally savedMainManager (the graph snapshot). version is the child-index path from head to the current action — [] is the root. `goto` consumes exactly that array.
concepts.created ids: Every action that creates something returns it in result.created: add_node -> nodeID, create_region/automation_curve/audio_clip -> regionID/curveID/clipID, create_note -> noteID, create_notes -> noteIDs, create_position -> positionID, add_arranger_track -> trackID+connectionID, sampler_add_sample -> sampleIndex, io_port_channel (add) -> connectionId+connectionIndex. Never guess an id.
concepts.capture: op capture takes {"target":"main"} (the node canvas), "node:<nodeID>" (just that node on the canvas, including live meters/spectra it draws — for a VST node with its editor open this captures the plugin editor window itself), or a window title / numeric id from the `windows` query, and replies with {target, format:"png", width, height, data:<base64 PNG>}. The reply is produced after the next frame is rendered, so it is always fresh; it just arrives a frame later. Add "beat": N to hold the capture until the transport reaches that absolute beat (frame-synced, useful for transient stems); if the transport is stopped it captures immediately. Use it to see the actual UI. Open a VST editor with the `window` op: {"op":"window","open":"vst_editor","nodeID":N} (add "closeEditor":true to hide it).
concepts.windows: The `windows` query lists the main canvas plus every expanded window (title, id, sdlWindowID, size, visibility). The `window` op opens/closes them: open preferences, undo_tree, arranger (nodeID), patcher (nodeID), sample_editor (nodeID, sampleIndex) or piano_roll (nodeID, regionID); close by title or id. Open a window, then capture it by title.
concepts.pitch tokens: create_note / create_notes accept either an explicit int[][] vector or a token string that resolves to the same vector: m69 or midi:69 (MIDI note -> 2^((n-69)/12)), e7/12 or edo:7/12 (EDO steps), 3/2 or ji:3/2 or ratio:3/2 (just ratio, prime-factorised into the positional vector), h9 or harmonic:9 (harmonic 9 octave-reduced to 9/8). Bare integers are MIDI notes, bare fractions are ratios. Tokens are exact vectors, so they work identically in EDO and harmonic-lattice regions.
concepts.note rhythm offsets: The first slot is prime 2, so a single pair [[num,den]] means exactly num/den beats (log2(2^(num/den))). Placing notes on sixteenths is therefore [[1,4]], [[2,4]], [[3,4]], [[5,4]], [[9,4]], ... and a bar line is [[9,1]] for beat 9. Later slots add log2(prime_i)^(num/den) over primes 3,5,7,...
concepts.sampler: A Sampler has one slot per loaded sample, in slot order. The Master event input (port 0) selects the slot from the note number: note 69 + index plays slot `index` (clamped to the last slot); any fraction is ignored (round-to-nearest). Each slot also has its own event input `S<n> Evt` (ports 1..n) that selects that slot regardless of pitch, and one stereo waveform output `S<n> Out` (port ids 0..n-1). Playback pitch is note - the slot's pitch parameter (default 69), so set a slot's pitch param to the note number you will play for native rate. Each slot contributes 9 consecutive params starting at index slotIndex*9: volume, pitch, pan, offset, cutoff, attack, decay, sustain, release.
concepts.audio routing: The Output node (id 0) has one waveform input per output channel and copies channel 0 of each input to that channel — connect to both inputs for stereo. Bus (nodeType 16) SUMS every connected waveform input into one output whose width is the widest source; use it to mix several cables. Mixer (nodeType 17) feeds one audio input into a list of serial node chains and sums their outputs, using the widest chain output as its channel count and delaying shorter chains so they stay latency-aligned. Merger (nodeType 2) does not mix: it places each input on its own output channel. Duplicator (nodeType 18) is the opposite of Splitter: one waveform input, eight outputs, and every output carries a full copy of the input at the input's channel width. Splitter (nodeType 3) instead divides input channels across its eight mono outputs. An unconnected output or input is silent.
concepts.self-description: `help` returns these concepts plus indexes. `describe_action` / `describe_query` / `describe_op` return one entry in full, including parameters and a worked example. Prefer those over guessing.
